correctness.rationale: For every integer t>=1, fixed-hub proper four-colour states factor into t independent six-cycles, giving exactly 4*6^t vertices and 4*t*6^t within-layer edges. Between any two hub colours there are exactly 2^t eligible synchronized gateways and hence 6*2^t additional edges. In each of the two six-cycles the two gateway states are antipodal; the sum of the two possible via-gateway per-petal costs equals six, so one gateway incurs at most three leaf recolourings. This gives an all-pairs upper bound 3t+1. A uniform reversed-petal colouring with a different hub colour forces at least three recolourings per petal plus one at the hub and an explicit path attains the bound. Proper three-colour states are all isolated. The standalone independent-adjacency enumeration checks t=1..5 and local gateway identities but is supplementary, not the proof.

value.rationale: The minimum palette chi=3 is entirely frozen, yet the smallest additional palette is connected, so the precise transition matters for dynamic scheduling/recolouring. This natural unbounded chordal family has a sharp linear recolouring budget 3t+1, a matching explicit worst-case obstruction, a canonical product-and-gateway state model, and exact total and hub-edge counts. The information is structural and optimal, not a routine instance count or small constant gain.
